UCR Student Success Center

A campus crossroads became common ground.

A student center works when students actually cross paths. The landscape makes that happen.

Porous, multi-level circulation draws people through, and carefully placed outdoor rooms give them reasons to stay. Campus planting palettes and paving let the new center belong to Riverside from day one.

Client
University of California, Riverside
Location
Riverside, California
Completion
2022
Services
Landscape architecture, hardscape design, campus integration

Belonging by design

The brief asked for a new building. The site asked for a meeting place. Multi-level pathways stitch the center into the routes students already walk, and the planting comes from the campus's own palette, so nothing about it reads as new for the sake of new.

The outdoor rooms work as hard as the interior ones.

Before a line is drawn, we find the story.

From the first conceptual sketch to construction, our commitment runs through Process Oriented Design. Every site holds a story. POD is how we uncover it, and how we build it with purpose for people and the environment.

  1. 01

    Listen

    Every place already has people who know it best.

    The design journey begins in dialogue: community, client, and our design and engineering collaborators around one table. What we hear shapes the brief before anything is drawn.

  2. 02

    Find the story

    A site is a narrative waiting to be read.

    History, ecology, and daily life give each place its plot. Exploring the story embedded in the site is the crucial first move; the design grows from what is already true.

  3. 03

    Draw by hand

    The hand finds what the survey cannot.

    We sketch before we model. Drawing keeps the design honest, human, and open to change, and the sketches stay on the table through every conversation.

  4. 04

    Build together

    Construction continues the conversation.

    We stay close through documentation and construction, and the community stays involved until opening day.

POD, drawn out

How we build

  • Native and drought tolerant planting

    Planting that thrives in the climate we are getting, not the one we had.

  • Stormwater and groundwater recharge

    Ground that drinks the rain. Stormwater is a resource, not a nuisance.

  • Recycled and local materials

    Materials sourced close to home, with second lives built in.

  • Cooling and shade

    Design that prevents solar heat gain and gives every visitor somewhere cool to be.

Design as a civic act.

We believe urban open space is the pinnacle of democratic practice. Everyone, regardless of origin, color, religion, or interest, can be there together.

HKLA is a full service landscape architecture practice in Los Angeles, founded in 2012. Three principles guide the work: collaborative design, contextual exploration of landscape as art, and innovative urban ecology. The goal is simple: harmony between people and nature.

Boutique by design. Small enough that every project gets our best people. Experienced enough that nothing surprises us.

Hongjoo Kim

Founding Principal, ASLA

Hongjoo founded HKLA in 2012. He holds a Master of Landscape Architecture from the Harvard Graduate School of Design and brings nearly three decades of practice to public work across Southern California.
